raw_response: This study develops a machine learning model to predict water potability, addressing the critical global need for safe drinking water. Using physical and chemical parameters (pH, turbidity, total dissolved solids, conductivity, hardness) from diverse sources, several binary classification algorithms—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and SVM—were trained and compared. The Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved the highest accuracy at 82.3%. Feature analysis identified pH, total dissolved solids, and hardness as the most significant predictors of drinkability. The resulting model offers a scalable, deployable tool for real-time water quality assessment, demonstrating machine learning’s potential to support public health decision-making and improve access to safe water.
